conjs: Conjecture: a(n) with n >= 0 can never be a perfect power. Also, the sequence (a(n+1)/a(n))_{n>=0} is strictly decreasing (to the limit 1). - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Dec 27 2024
gfs: 256*(1 - lambda + lambda^2)^3/(lambda^2 * (1 - lambda)^2) where lambda is the elliptic modular function (A115977). - _Seiichi Manyama_, Jul 30 2017
A000521.name: Coefficients of modular function j as power series in q = e^(2 Pi i t). Another name is the elliptic modular invariant J(tau).

conjs: Conjecture: G.f.: 1 = Sum_{n>=0} a(n+1)*A000108(n)*x^n*Sum_{k>=0} C(2*n+k,k)^2*(-x)^k. Compare with the following g.f of the Catalan numbers (A000108): 1 = Sum_{n>=0} A000108(n)*x^n*Sum_{k>=0} C(2*n+k,k)*(-x)^k. - _Paul D. Hanna_, Oct 10 2010
A002190.name: Sum_{n>=0} a(n)*x^n/n!^2 = -log(BesselJ(0,2*sqrt(x))).

conjs: Conjecture: The n-th derivative of Gamma(x+1) at x = 0 has a(n+1) terms. For example, d^4/dx^4_(x = 0) Gamma(x+1) = 8*eulergamma*zeta(3) + eulergamma^4 + eulergamma^2*Pi^2 + 3*Pi^4/20 which has a(5) = 4 terms. - _David Ulgenes_, Dec 05 2023
A038348.name: Expansion of (1/(1-x^2))*Product_{m>=0} 1/(1-x^(2m+1)).

conjs: Conjecture: a(n)+a(n+1)+a(n+2) = 8*n-1; or a(n) = 8*(n-2)-a(n-1)-a(n-2)-1, n>3, with a(1)=0, a(2)=2, a(3)=5. - _L. Edson Jeffery_, Sep 02 2014
A047618.name: Numbers that are congruent to {0, 2, 5} mod 8.

conjs: Conjecture:  let b(n) be the number of subsets S of {1,2,...,n} having more than one element such that (sum of least two elements of S) > max(S).  Then b(0) = b(1) = 0 and b(n+2) = a(n+1) for n >= 0. - _Clark Kimberling_ Sep 27 2022
A053599.name: Number of nonempty subsequences {s(k)} of 1..n such that the difference sequence is palindromic.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+1) = (1/(n+1))*Sum_{k=0..floor(n/4)} binomial(n+1, n-4*k)*binomial(n+k, n) (compare to the formula from _Peter Bala_ in A215340). - _Joerg Arndt_, Apr 01 2019
A063019.name: Reversion of y - y^2 + y^3 - y^4.

conjs: Conjectures: -1 < a(n) < n+2; If a(n) = n+1 then a(n+1) = 0; All integers >1 occur in the sequence; For each c in [0,1] there exists a subsequence a(i_j) with (a(i_j)+1)/(i_j+3)-> c, j->infinity.
A065806.name: A pseudo-random sequence.

conjs: As Catalan's conjecture is now proved, n=8=2^3, n+1=9=3^2 is the only solution for a(n+1) = a(n) = 0.
A069584.name: a(n) = n - largest perfect power <= n.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n) = 4*n + pa(n mod 4), where pa(k) = 0,3,4,3 for k=0,1,2,3 respectively; lim_{n->infinity} a(n)/n = 4; a(n)/n >= 4; a(n+4) = a(n) + 16. - _Jerzy R Borysowicz_, Jan 16 2022
A072834.name: Exponents occurring in expansion of F_8(q^2).

conjs: Conjectures : (1) a(n+1)-a(n) = 0 or 1; (2) lim n ->infinity a(n)/n = 2/3; (3) 1/2 < (3a(n)-2n)/Log(n) <3/2 for any n > 1000. Does lim n -> infinity (3a(n)-2n)/Log(n) = 1 ?
A072894.name: Let c(k) be defined as follows: c(1)=1, c(2)=n, c(k+2) = c(k+1)/2 + c(k)/2 if c(k+1) and c(k) have the same parity; c(k+2) = c(k+1)/2 + c(k)/2 + 1/2 otherwise; a(n) = limit_{ k -> infinity} c(k).

conjs: Conjecture 1: Define the sequences (A(n): n >= 1) and (B(n): n >= 1) by A(n+1) = n^2/A(n) + 1 for n >= 2 with A(1) = infinity and A(2) = 1, and B(n+1) = n^2/B(n) + 1 for n >= 3 with B(1) = 0, B(2) = infinity, and B(3) = 1. Then a(n) = denominator(A(n)), b(n) = numerator(A(n)), c(n) = numerator(B(n)), and d(n) = denominator(B(n)) (assuming infinity = 1/0). Also, gcd(a(n), d(n)) = 1.
A075830.name: Let u(1) = x and u(n+1) = (n^2/u(n)) + 1 for n >= 1; then a(n) is such that u(n) = (b(n)*x + c(n))/(a(n)*x + d(n)) (in lowest terms) and a(n), b(n), c(n), d(n) are positive integers.

conjs: Conjectures: Is a(n) monotonically increasing for n > 4? Does lim{n->inf} a(n)/a(n+1) = 0.5? - _Ryan Propper_, Jan 04 2008
A078671.name: Number of times the n-th prime appears among the decimal digits of 2^(2^n) + 1, the Fermat numbers.

conjs: Proof of conjecture: if d(n) = log_2(a(n+1)-a(n)), we have d(0)=0, d(1)=1, d(n)=d(n-1)+d(n-2), so d(n) = Fibonacci(n). - _Robert Israel_, Oct 25 2017
A079429.name: a(0) = 2, a(1) = 3, a(2) = 5; a(n) = a(n-1) + [a(n-1)-a(n-2)] * [a(n-2)-a(n-3)].

conjs: Conjecture: -(n+1)*a(n+1) + a(n) + n^2*(n+2)*a(n-1) = 0. - _R. J. Mathar_, Sep 27 2012, corrected for offset 1 by _Robert Israel_, Dec 26 2018
A080958.name: a(n) = n!*(2/1 - 3/2 + 4/3 - ... + s*(n+1)/n), where s = (-1)^(n+1).

conjs: Conjecture: log(a(n+1))/log(a(n)) -> 2. The 9th term has 69 digits, the 10th term has 140 digits. The decimal expansion of the continued fraction: [0;2,2,9,91,14201,252238179,...] = 0.404250350307436947086987047594...
A081086.name: Smallest partial quotients of an infinite simple continued fraction such that the fractional remainders sum to unity.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+1) >= a(n). Comments from _Don Reble_, Nov 13 2005: The conjecture is plainly true. In fact, a(n+1)-a(n) = 0 or 1. Also a(A091072(n)) = n; a(A091072(n)+1) = n+1.
A088023.name: Set a(1) = 1. Then take the list of defined initial terms, reverse their order, add 1, 2, 3, ... to the reversed list in succession and append this new list to the right of the previously defined terms. Repeat this process indefinitely.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+1) = (n mod 2) + Sum_{k=0..infinity} (4*5^k*(floor(n/5^(k+1)) mod 2)). - _Charlie Neder_, May 25 2019
A093348.name: A 5-fractal "castle" starting with 0.

A098926.name: Permanent of the (0,1)-matrix with ij-th entry equal to zero iff (i=1,j=1),(i=1,j=2),(i=1,j=3),(i=2,j=3),(i=3,j=3),... In other words, the ij-th entry of the matrix is zero iff it is on the path which start from the entry (i=1,j=1) and moves in the matrix alternating 3 steps to the right to 3 steps down.

conjs: Conjecture: For n >= 0, (-1)^n * a(n+1) is the numerator of the n-th term of the Taylor expansion of 1/(1 + sin(x)) around x = 0. [This is based on the fact that (sec(x) + tan(x))' = 1/(1 + sin(-x)). _Clark Kimberling_ in A279107 states my conjecture as a fact, but no proof or reference is given.] - _Petros Hadjicostas_, Oct 06 2019
A099612.name: Numerators of the coefficients in the Taylor expansion of sec(x) + tan(x) around x=0.

conjs: Conjecture: For n >= 0, (-1)^n * a(n+1)/(n+1) is the denominator of the n-th term of the Taylor expansion of 1/(1 + sin(x)) around x = 0. [This is based on the fact that (sec(x) + tan(x))' = 1/(1 + sin(-x)). Cf. also the comments in A099612 and A279107.] - _Petros Hadjicostas_, Oct 06 2019
A099617.name: Denominators of the coefficients in the Taylor expansion of sec(x) + tan(x) around x=0.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+1) is the number of distinct subsets S of {0,1,2,...,n} such that the sumset S+S does not contain n. - _Michael Chu_, Oct 05 2021. _Andrew Howroyd_, Nov 20 2021: The conjecture is true: If there are m pairs of numbers that add to n then inclusion/exclusion gives sum(k=0, m, binomial(m,k)*(-1)^k*2^(2*m-2*k)) as the number of sets that don't contain any of those pairs which equals 3^m. For even n , n/2 cannot be included in any set.
A108411.name: a(n) = 3^floor(n/2). Powers of 3 repeated.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+15)==0 (mod 30) for n > 4. - _Robert G. Wilson v_, Jul 21 2005
A109926.name: Least k such that k-2^r is prime for n values of r. Index of the first occurrence of n in A109925.

conjs: Conjecture. a(1)=0 and, for n>1, a(n+1)=a(n)+d(n), where d(n) is defined as follows: d=0,0,0,1,0 for n=1,...,5 and, for n>5, d(n)=d(n-2)+1 if n=6k or n=6k+4, d(n)=d(n-2) if n=6k+1 or n=6k+3, d(n)=d(n-2)+2Floor[n/6] if n=6k+2 and d(n)=d(n-5) if n=6k+5.
gfs: for number of partitions p of n such that max(p)-min(p) = m is Sum_{k>0} x^(2*k+m)/Product_{i=0..m} (1-x^(k+i)). - _Vladeta Jovovic_, Jul 04 2007
A128508.name: Number of partitions p of n such that max(p) - min(p) = 3.

conjs: In general, we can conjecture that the Hankel transform of h(n) of a(n+1), where a(n)=if(n=0,1,if(n=1,1,if(n=2,1,r*a(n-1)+s*sum{k=0..n-2, a(k)*a(n-1-k)}))), satisfies the generalized Somos-4 recurrence h(n)=(s^2*h(n-1)*h(n-3)+s^3*(2*s+r-2)*h(n-2)^2)/h(n-4).
A160702.name: Sequence such that the Hankel transform of a(n+1) satisfies a generalized Somos-4 recurrence.

conjs: Examples relating to the conjecture: Since A179238 has two recursive multipliers, we can extract the sequence A179237: (1, 2, 13, 80, 493, 3038,...) = convergents of A179238 such that a(n+1) = 2*a(n) + a(n-1). The convergent of this sequence = 1/(sqrt(10) - 3) = 6.16227766, ... = a, where 1/a = 0.1622776, ... the convergent to the palindromic continued fraction [6,6,6,...]. Then letting 1/a = tan(A), then tan(2A) = 1/3, rational. Similarly, taking a = 6.16227766, ... = tan(A), then tan(2A) = -1/3, rational, with a and 1/a irrational.
A179238.name: Numerators in convergents to infinitely repeating period 3 palindromic continued fraction [1,2,1,...].

conjs: Conjecture: The sequence a(n+1)/a(n) (n = 0,1,...) is strictly decreasing to the limit 3+2*sqrt(2), and the sequence a(n+1)^(1/(n+1))/a(n)^(1/n) (n = 1,2,3,..) is strictly increasing to the limit 1.
A180364.name: a(n) = sum_{k=0..n} C(n,k)*C(n+k,k)*(2*k+1)^2, where C(m,k) denotes the binomial coefficient m!/(k!*(m-k)!).

A189281.name: Number of permutations p of 1,2,...,n satisfying p(i+2) - p(i) <> 2 for all 1 <= i <= n-2.

A195806.name: Number of triangular of a 5 X 5 X 5 0..n arrays with all rows and diagonals having the same length having the same sum, with corners zero.

conjs: If the conjecture is true, then, for n >= 0, A007814(a(n+1)) = A007814(n!) + n.
A202367.name: LCM of denominators of the coefficients of polynomials Q^(2)_m(n) defined by the recursion Q^(2)_0(n)=1; for m >= 1, Q^(2)_m(n) = Sum_{i=1..n} i^2*Q^(2)_(m-1)(i).

conjs: In contrast to this conjecture, for the sequence of the positive integers (A=A000027) there are infinitely many n for which A(n) + A(n+1) + ... + A(n+k) is composite for every k>=0 (cf. A089306, A077654).
A256461.name: Smallest k such that A098550(n) + A098550(n+1) + ... + A098550(n+k) is prime, or -1 if there is no such k.

conjs: It is conjectured that for all n, a(n) = 0 implies that 2n+1 = a(n+1) is prime, cf. A186254. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261302.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 2n+1)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that a(n) = 0 implies that 3n+2 = a(n+1) is prime, for all n > 2, cf. A186255. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261303.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 3n+2)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that a(n) = 0 implies that 4n+3 = a(n+1) is prime, cf. A186256. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261304.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 4n+3)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that a(n) = 0 implies that 5n+4 = a(n+1) is prime for n > 2, cf. A186256. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261305.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 5*n+4)), u(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that for all n, a(n) = 0 implies that a(n+1) = 6n+5 is prime, cf. A186258. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261306.name: a(n+1) = abs((n) - gcd(a(n), 6*n+5)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that for all n > 2, a(n) = 0 implies that 7n+6 = a(n+1) is prime, cf. A186259. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261307.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 7*n+6)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that for all n, a(n) = 0 implies that 8n+7 = a(n+1) is prime, cf. A186260. (This is the sequence {u(n)} mentioned there.)
A261308.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 8n+7)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: It is conjectured that for all n, a(n) = 0 implies that a(n+1) = 10n+9 is prime, cf. A186263.
A261310.name: a(n+1) = abs(a(n) - gcd(a(n), 10n+9)), a(1) = 1.

conjs: Conjecture: this is a monotonic sequence. For n = 0, 1, 3, 4, 8, 12, 17, 23, 41 & 59, a(n) = a(n+1).
A262669.name: Consider the Farey sequence of order n, F_n, and that the average distance between any two adjacent pairs in F_n is 1/A002088(n). Then a(n) is the number of adjacent pairs whose difference is less than the average.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+1) = Sum_{j=0..n/2} A027907(n-j,2*j), n >= 0.
gfs: A(x) = x*(1-x-x^2)*B(x), where B is g.f. of A077864.
A262735.name: Expansion of x*(1-x-x^2)/((1-x)*(1-x-2*x^2-x^3)).

A269021.name: Number of permutations of [2n] containing an increasing subsequence of length n.

A339987.name: The number of labeled graphs on 2n vertices that share the same degree sequence as any unrooted binary tree on 2n vertices.

conjs: Conjecture: a(n+1)/a(n) tends to d = 5.566315770083119..., where d is the real root of the equation d^3 - 4*d^2 - 8*d - 4 = 0. - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Nov 28 2023
A367558.name: Number of knight paths from opposite corners of an n X n matrix, using only turns that lower Manhattan distance.

conjs: Conjecture: Let d(n) = a(n+1) - a(n) for n >= 0.  Then d(n) = 1 for infinitely many n, and (d(n)) is unbounded.
A373097.name: a(n) = a[n/r] + a[n/r^2] + a[n/r^3] + ... , where a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1, r = 3/2, and [ ] = floor.

conjs: Suppose that s = (s(n)) and t = (t(n)) are sequences of numbers and r > 0. The lower (r)-midsequence of s and t is given by u = floor(r*(s + t)); the upper r-midsequence of s and t is given by v = ceiling(r*(s + t)). If s and t are linearly recurrent and r is rational, then u and v are linearly recurrent. Conjecture: a(n+2) = A111097(n+2) for n>=0.
A389142.name: Lower (1/3)-midsequence of square numbers and triangular numbers; see Comments.
